_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); orders, revenue and margin signals; the listing and short-history bounds rules

pit_profile.why: Baker Hughes: 'an energy technology company with a diversified portfolio of technologies and services that span the energy and industrial value chain'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'may curtail production and demand for hydrocarbons such as oil and natural gas by shifting demand towards an investment in relatively lower carbon emitting energy sources and alternative energy solutions'; 'Failure to effectively and timely execute our energy transition strategy could have an adverse effect on the demand for our technologies and services' (its own FY2021 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' spending on exploration, development and production through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services and equipment company does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: Baker Hughes: 'an energy technology company with a diversified portfolio of technologies and services that span the energy and industrial value chain'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'may curtail production and demand for hydrocarbons such as oil and natural gas by shifting demand towards an investment in relatively lower carbon emitting energy sources and alternative energy solutions'; 'Failure to effectively and timely execute our energy transition strategy could have an adverse effect on the demand for our technologies and services' (its own FY2021 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' spending on exploration, development and production through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services and equipment company does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.29x; +26% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.38; conservative 2yr +21%.

BEAR.desc: Flat EPS (no EPS change in FY18-FY18 to measure: the 0% cap); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +3.5%/yr (Q1 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 4.5-yr ex-FY17 ex-FY19 ex-FY20 ex-FY21 median

BULL.desc: EPS +3.5%/yr (no FY18-FY18 CAGR to measure: BASE's rate); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +3.5%/yr (no 2-yr run in FY18-FY18: BULL's rate); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: BKR (retrospective, 2022-07-08) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.29x (8.7% downside to Bear $26 / +30.0% upside to Bull $37) | Adj composite 3.07 vs market 3.45: gap -0.38 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +27% above the EPP floor $22 (50x FY22E $0.45) | Conservative 2-yr case: +20.9% total (+10.4%/yr) | At 63.3x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $38 sits above the BULL case; orders +50.6% and revenue +1.1% in Q1 2022, forward revenues +1.1% (no Q2 2022 revenue guide, Q1 2022 revenue as reported); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.
